title: Beyond Memory Majority: Latent-Source Reasoning for Multi-Agent Memory Arbitration
abstract: arXiv:2608.19701v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term multi-agent systems continuously accumulate the memories produced by different agents. Existing memory methods typically treat retrieved memories as independent evidence and combine them through voting or weighting. However, this independence assumption often fails in multi-agent settings: memories written by different agents may inherit the same upstream source or shared bias, causing correlated evidence to be repeatedly counted and creating a false majority. We term this failure mode \textit{Memory Correlation Bias}. To address the issue, we propose the \textbf{C}orrelation-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{M}emory \textbf{A}rbitration (CAMA) framework that jointly decouples retrieved memories and recovers missing independent evidence. We model the retrieved memories as query-conditioned evidence groups and combine neural dependency inference with provenance-based symbolic priors to estimate the effective number of independent evidence

translated_title: 超越记忆多数原则：多智能体记忆仲裁中的潜在源推理
translated_abstract: 长期多智能体系统会持续积累由不同智能体产生的记忆。现有的记忆方法通常将检索到的记忆视为独立证据，并通过投票或加权方式进行组合。然而，这种独立性假设在多智能体环境中常常失效：不同智能体编写的记忆可能继承相同的上游来源或共享偏见，导致相关证据被重复计数，从而形成虚假的多数。我们将这种失败模式称为“记忆相关性偏差”。为解决这一问题，我们提出了**相关性感知记忆仲裁**（CAMA）框架，该框架联合解耦检索到的记忆并恢复缺失的独立证据。我们将检索到的记忆建模为查询条件下的证据组，并结合神经依赖推理与基于来源的符号先验来估计独立证据的有效数量。
tldr: 本文提出了一种相关性感知记忆仲裁框架，通过解耦检索记忆并恢复缺失的独立证据，解决了多智能体系统中因证据相关性导致的虚假多数问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a correlation-aware memory arbitration framework that decouples retrieved memories and recovers missing independent evidence, addressing the false majority issue caused by evidence correlation in multi-agent systems.
